notes.sowing: Sow directly after your last frost, once the soil is about {c:18}, only {cm:0.3} deep, since deeper sowing cuts germination. Seed comes up in 1 to 2 weeks. Thin to {cm:30} to {cm:60} apart.
notes.care: Full sun and poor to average soil; rich soil or fertilizer gives floppy stems and late, sparse flowers, so do not feed. Tall plants may need staking. Deadhead, or cut plants back to {cm:30} to {cm:45} for a fresh flush. Self-sows readily.
notes.harvest: Flowers start 2 to 3 months from sowing and peak in late summer as the days shorten. Cut stems when the buds are just opening. Bees, butterflies, hoverflies and lacewings visit the flowers.
